# technitium_record_tlsa (Resource)

Manages a single `TLSA` record in an authoritative zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_zone" "tlsa_home" {
  zone = "tlsa.example.com"
}

resource "technitium_record_tlsa" "https" {
  zone                              = technitium_zone.tlsa_home.zone
  domain                            = "_443._tcp.tlsa.example.com"
  tlsa_certificate_usage            = "DANE-EE"
  tlsa_selector                     = "SPKI"
  tlsa_matching_type                = "SHA2-256"
  tlsa_certificate_association_data = "D4A7E3B0C44298FC1C149AFBF4C8996FB92427AE41E4649B934CA495991B7852"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The record's domain name, for example `www.example.com`. Use the zone name for a record at the zone apex.
- `tlsa_certificate_association_data` (String) The certificate data to match, as a hex string.
- `tlsa_certificate_usage` (String) How the certificate is checked: `PKIX-TA`, `PKIX-EE`, `DANE-TA` or `DANE-EE`.
- `tlsa_matching_type` (String) How the data is matched: `Full`, `SHA2-256` or `SHA2-512`.
- `tlsa_selector` (String) What is matched: `Cert` for the whole certificate or `SPKI` for its public key.
- `zone` (String) The authoritative zone that holds the record.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Comments stored with the record.
- `disable` (Boolean) Disable the record without deleting it. A DNSSEC signed zone refuses disabled records, and a zone that holds one cannot be signed. Defaults to `false`.
- `expiry_ttl` (Number) Deletes the record automatically this many seconds after it was last modified. Terraform then creates it again on the next apply. Defaults to `0`, which keeps the record.
- `ttl` (Number) The record TTL in seconds. The records at one name and type share one TTL, so a value different from theirs is refused, and changing it on a record that has theirs changes it on all of them. Defaults to their TTL, or else to the default record TTL in the server settings.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# zone/domain/tlsa_certificate_usage/tlsa_selector/tlsa_matching_type/tlsa_certificate_association_data
terraform import technitium_record_tlsa.https tlsa.example.com/_443._tcp.tlsa.example.com/DANE-EE/SPKI/SHA2-256/D4A7E3B0C44298FC1C149AFBF4C8996FB92427AE41E4649B934CA495991B7852
```
